# Volume 3 — Chapter XXXVIII False Dawn

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“Only think—seven days from tonight I will find myself in Brierley—what a charming prospect!” exclaimed Nell, leaning above the crate where she was storing away the quilts belonging to Mrs. Agatha Sowerby. “On the other hand, only think—seven days from tonight I will have departed eternally from Tabby’s Place—what a dreadful prospect!”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0000 }

“I ponder whether the spirit of every laugh we shared will resonate in the youthful reveries of Miss Tabby and Miss Maria,” Cressy conjectured.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0001 }

Miss Tabby and Miss Maria were returning to their residence, following their journey across nearly the entirety of the inhabited world.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0002 }

“We will return during May’s second week,” Miss Tabby had written. “Though Tabby’s Place might feel somewhat tiny following Karnak's Hall of the Kings, I have always disliked large dwellings. Besides, returning home will be a great relief. Beginning your travels at an advanced age often leads to overdoing it, given the awareness that little time remains, and the habit easily takes hold. Maria, I fear, will never find contentment again.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0003 }

“I shall leave here my fancies and dreams to bless the next comer,” Nell remarked, casting a longing glance across the blue room—that lovely blue room in which she had passed three years of such joy. Upon her knees by its window she had offered her prayers, and leaning out from it she had observed the sun setting beyond the pine trees. She had listened as fall rain dashed against the glass, and she had greeted the robins of springtime on its ledge. She pondered whether previous dreams might linger in rooms—whether, upon departing eternally from the place where a person had experienced happiness, pain, laughter, and tears, a part of her, unseen and ungraspable, but fully actual all the same, might linger like an echoing recollection.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0004 }

“I believe,” Cressy remarked, “that any space in which a person experiences dreams, grief, joy, and life grows bound up with those occurrences and gains a distinct character. Were I to step into this room half a century in the future, I know it would whisper ‘Nell, Nell’ in my direction. We’ve shared such wonderful moments in this spot, sweetie! All the conversations, laughs, and warm, friendly gatherings! Oh, goodness! My wedding to Ez takes place in June, and I am certain my joy will be absolute. Yet at this very moment, my wish is for this delightful Wexcombe existence to continue without end.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0005 }

“I am sufficiently illogical at this moment to desire that as well,” Nell conceded. “Regardless of whatever more profound happiness might await us in the future, we will never experience this precise charming, carefree life we have shared here again. Cressy, it has ended permanently.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0006 }

“What will be done with Smudge?” Cressy inquired, just as that favored feline stepped into the space.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0007 }

“I shall bring him to my house to be with Joseph and the Sarah-cat,” stated Aunt Euphemia, pursuing Smudge. “Separating those cats after they have mastered coexisting would be a pity. Cats and people find that a difficult lesson to master.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0008 }

“I regret having to give up Smudge,” Nell stated sorrowfully, “however, bringing him to Grey Shutters would serve no purpose. Cats are loathed by Thirza, and Robin would torment him incessantly. Furthermore, my time at home will likely be short. The position of principal at the Eastmere High School has been extended to me.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0009 }

“Will you be accepting it?” Cressy asked.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0010 }

“I—I have not made up my mind yet,” Nell replied, flushing with confusion.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0011 }

Cressy gave an understanding nod. Of course, it was impossible to finalize Nell’s future until Cyril had expressed himself. He would do so shortly—there was certainly no uncertainty about it. Nor was there any uncertainty that Nell’s response would be “yes” once he asked “Will you please?” Nell viewed the situation herself with a composure that was rarely disturbed. She possessed a deep love for Cyril. To be sure, it differed from her initial expectations of love. Yet Nell questioned herself tiredly, did anything in existence resemble a person's mental picture of it? It mirrored the previous diamond disenchantment of her youth—matching the exact letdown she experienced upon first beholding the cold gleam rather than the violet magnificence she had expected. “That’s not my idea of a diamond,” she had declared. Nevertheless, Cyril was a wonderful man and their life together would be filled with great happiness, despite the absence of a certain nameless excitement from her existence. When Cyril arrived that night and requested that Nell join him for a stroll through the park, all the residents at Tabby’s Place understood his intentions; and all of them understood, or believed they understood, how Nell would reply.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0012 }

“Nell is an extremely lucky girl,” Aunt Euphemia remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0013 }

“I guess that’s right,” Mabel remarked with a shrug of her shoulders. “Cyril is a good guy and everything like that. However, he actually lacks any real substance.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0014 }

“Mabel Colby, that sounds remarkably like a jealous comment,” Aunt Euphemia said in a tone of rebuke.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0015 }

“It does—yet I entertain no jealousy,” Mabel stated placidly. “I hold affection for Nell, and Cyril pleases me. Everyone asserts that her marriage will be a splendid one, and at present even Mrs. Lisle finds her delightful. Everything appears as though it were fashioned in paradise, though I harbor my reservations. Take whatever you can from that, Aunt Euphemia.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0016 }

Cyril requested that Nell become his wife inside the small pavilion located by the harbor shore, the very place of their conversation during the rainy day when they first met. Nell considered his choice of that location to be extremely romantic. Furthermore, the phrasing of his proposal was so exquisite that it seemed as though it might have been transcribed from a Deportment of Courtship and Marriage, just as a lover of Opal Pettigrew had once done. Its total impression was entirely perfect. It possessed sincerity as well. That Cyril truly intended his words was beyond question. No discordant tone existed that might disrupt the symphony. Nell believed that a head-to-toe shudder of excitement should be coming over her. Yet it was not; an awful composure possessed her. As Cyril waited for her response, her lips parted so she could utter her momentous yes. At that instant—a shaking came over her as though she were recoiling from the edge of a cliff. A moment arrived for her in which a person understands, as if struck by a dazzling burst of insight, far more than all earlier years combined have revealed. She yanked her hand away from Cyril’s.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0017 }

“Oh, I am unable to marry you—I am unable—I am unable,” she exclaimed, hysterically.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0018 }

Cyril grew pale, looking quite silly as well. He had been exceedingly confident, though he could hardly be faulted for it.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0019 }

“In what way do you intend that?” he gasped out.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0020 }

“I am saying that marrying you is impossible for me,” Nell reiterated frantically. “I believed it was possible—yet it isn’t.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0021 }

“What is the reason you are unable to?” inquired Cyril, with greater composure.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0022 }

“Because—you do not matter enough to me.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0023 }

A red flush appeared on Cyril’s face.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0024 }

“Then you have merely been entertaining yourself throughout these past two years?” he uttered unhurriedly.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0025 }

“No, no, I haven’t,” poor Nell panted. Oh, what way was there for her to clarify? Clarification was impossible for her. Certain matters simply defy all explanation. “I believed I was fond of you—I really did—yet now I am certain I am not.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0026 }

“My life has been destroyed by you,” Cyril said with bitterness.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0027 }

“Pardon me,” begged Nell in misery, her cheeks burning and her eyes smarting.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0028 }

Cyril turned around and spent a few minutes gazing toward the sea. By the time he returned to Nell, his face had grown extremely pale once more.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0029 }

“Is there no hope you can offer me?” he asked.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0030 }

In silence, Nell gave a shake of her head.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0031 }

“Well then—farewell,” Cyril uttered. “It is beyond my comprehension—it is impossible for me to accept that you aren't the lady I thought you were. However, upbraiding one another is useless now. No other female will ever have my affection. I am grateful to you for your companionship, if nothing else. Farewell, Nell.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0032 }

“Good-bye,” Nell stammered. After Cyril departed, she remained seated in the pavilion for many minutes, observing a pale fog stealthily and unyieldingly drifting toward the shore up the harbor. She was experiencing her moment of degradation, self-disdain, and embarrassment. Their surges swept across her. Nevertheless, beneath every bit of it, lay a strange feeling of regained liberty.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0033 }

She stole inside Tabby’s Place during the twilight and retreated to her chamber. Nevertheless, Cressy was present upon the window seat.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0034 }

“Hold on,” uttered Nell, her cheeks reddening as she foresaw the moment. “Hold on until I tell you my news. Cressy, Cyril wanted me to be his wife-and I said no.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0035 }

“You—you turned him down?” Cressy asked with a blank expression.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0036 }

“Yes.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0037 }

“Nell Harcourt, have you lost your mind?”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0038 }

“I believe I do,” Nell uttered tiredly. “Oh, Cressy, please do not lecture me. You fail to comprehend.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0039 }

“I truly am baffled. For a pair of years, you have given Cyril Lisle every form of encouragement—only to inform me now that you turned him down. It means you were simply engaging in a disgraceful flirtation with him. Nell, I would never have expected such behavior from you.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0040 }

“It wasn’t flirtation on my part—until the very final moment, I truly believed my feelings were genuine—and after that—well, it simply became clear that becoming his wife was impossible for me.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0041 }

“It is my guess,” Cressy stated maliciously, “that his wealth was the reason you planned to wed him, but your higher nature intervened to stop you.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0042 }

“I didn’t. His money never crossed my mind. Oh, I cannot make you understand it, just as I was unable to make him understand.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0043 }

“Indeed, it seems to me that your treatment of Cyril has been disgraceful,” Cressy declared, annoyed. “He possesses good looks, intelligence, wealth, and virtue. What else could you desire?”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0044 }

“I desire a person who fits into my existence. He does not. Initially, his attractive appearance and skill at offering romantic praise swept me off my feet; and subsequently, I assumed I was required to be enamored since he represented my dark-eyed perfection.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0045 }

“Not knowing what I want makes me bad, yet your behavior is even worse,” Cressy stated.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0046 }

“My own mind is well known to me,” Nell objected. “My mind alters, which is the problem, forcing me to become familiar with it once more.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0047 }

“Well, I guess talking to you is completely pointless.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0048 }

“Cressy, there’s no necessity for that. My spirit is broken. Everything in the past has been ruined by this. It will be impossible for me to ponder the time at Wexcombe without remembering how I was humiliated tonight. I am despised by Cyril—as well as by you—and I hold myself in contempt.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0049 }

“You poor darling,” said Cressy, softening. “Just come over here and allow me to comfort you. I have no right to reprimand you. I would have wed Hector or Orlando had I not encountered Ez. Oh, Nell, matters are so tangled in actual life. They are not neatly defined and trimmed away, like they are in books.”
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0050 }

“I hope that no person will ever ask for my hand in marriage again for the rest of my life,” cried unfortunate Nell, deeply convinced that her words were true.
{: #nw-v03-c38-p0051 }
